name: Kiss It Goodbye
label: Revelation
lede: Two refugees from Deadguy and the rhythm section of Rorschach moved across the country to make one brutal album in Seattle, then broke up before their Sub Pop debut could come out.

eras.title: Deadguy, minus the politics
eras.text: Tim Singer and Keith Huckins walked out of Deadguy, New Jersey's noisiest band, and pulled in the bass-and-drums engine of Rorschach. They practiced like crazy in New York, then drove the whole operation to Seattle.

years.src: No Echo: Keith Huckins · Hex Records: Tim Singer · Wikipedia
years.h: Tim Singer and Keith Huckins quit Deadguy and form Kiss It Goodbye
years.p: Keith Huckins blames band politics. Tim Singer wanted to move to Seattle, and Huckins didn't care where they lived, so they recruited Rorschach's Thom Rusnak and Andrew Gormley and went.
years.xp: Before leaving the East Coast, the new band practiced hard, cut a demo called Be Afraid that got passed around New York, and played a run of New York shows. Singer says they hit the ground running once they reached Seattle.

years.h: Kiss It Goodbye record with Billy Anderson at Ironwood, Seattle
years.p: Kiss It Goodbye track their only album at Ironwood Studios in Seattle with producer Billy Anderson. Keith Huckins's reason for choosing Anderson was one word: [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]].

eras.title: Nine songs, then the floor at some kid's house
eras.text: She Loves Me, She Loves Me Not landed on Revelation and in the metal press at the same time. Then came touring with Unsane and Obituary, and the grind of the road cost the band the guitarist who'd started it.

years.src: Wikipedia · Revelation Records pressing history · No Echo
years.h: She Loves Me, She Loves Me Not · Revelation REV 58
years.p: Nine songs in 45 minutes, from Fire Drill at under two to Sick Day at eight and a half. Terrorizer ranked it No. 17 of 1997; it hit No. 13 on CMJ's Metal Top 25 that July.
years.xp:
The first vinyl run was 1,220 black and 317 clear. Tim Singer built his vocals from a phrase or two at practice rather than writing lyrics out in advance.

No Echo counts [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]] and [[Daughters|c9368a03-bf26-40b6-bdfa-9af8d10b568b]] among the bands it rubbed off on.
play: She Loves Me, She Loves Me Not

years.p: Kiss It Goodbye's two-song Revelation 7". The first pressing was just 100 copies on red vinyl, with a later run of 330 on gold.

years.h: Kiss It Goodbye tour with Unsane and Obituary
years.p: Kiss It Goodbye spend 1997 on the road with New York noise-rock band [[Unsane|db9cbc9e-65b6-4221-a847-75981feb1c6b]] and Florida death metal band [[Obituary|2e8ac3ed-2a89-4377-ba80-790106aba554]].

years.h: Keith Huckins quits Kiss It Goodbye; Demian Johnston joins
years.p: After the 1997 tours, guitarist Keith Huckins leaves Kiss It Goodbye. He was done driving twelve hours to play for fifteen people and sleep on a stranger's floor. Seattle's [[Demian Johnston|46dc5d39-ed27-41ed-9620-f7b88f035f80]] takes over.
years.xp:
Huckins told No Echo the novelty had simply worn off: long drives, tiny crowds, a floor at some random kid's house at the end of the night.

Johnston went on to [[Playing Enemy|61b0f945-ce01-4925-950e-fbc5ce389957]].

eras.title: The Sub Pop record nobody got
eras.text: Kiss It Goodbye recorded three songs for a Sub Pop EP, and then Tim Singer quit. The tapes waited, and Revelation put them out as a farewell.

years.h: Tim Singer leaves, and Kiss It Goodbye end
years.p: With three new songs recorded for Sub Pop, Tim Singer quits Kiss It Goodbye. Around 30, with marriage and young kids ahead, he felt hardcore bands weren't meant to go on into your thirties.

years.src: Wikipedia: Choke · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Choke: Kiss It Goodbye's lost Sub Pop EP, on Revelation
years.p: The three songs recorded in 1998 for Sub Pop finally come out on Revelation as a 7" and a five-song CD, with production by Matt Bayles and Billy Anderson.
years.xp: The CD adds earlier unreleased material from around the album sessions. The 7" ran 220 on purple vinyl, then 330 on orange.

eras.title: Two returns, one for a friend
eras.text: Kiss It Goodbye came back twice: a short West Coast run in 2012, and in 2025 the original album line-up in Brooklyn, playing to raise money for the family of New York hardcore promoter Rich Hall.

years.h: Kiss It Goodbye's 2012 West Coast reunion tour
years.p: Tim Singer and Thom Rusnak return with guitarist Alex Miller and drummer Neal Witmer. Revelation re-presses She Loves Me, She Loves Me Not on white vinyl, 560 copies, for the tour.
Tim Singer's newer band, with [[Dan Yemin|bfac6050-54c5-4b29-bb73-465c90e6e327]] on bass, releases Your Neighbors Are Failures on Equal Vision.

years.h: Kiss It Goodbye's album line-up plays for Rich Hall at Warsaw
years.p: Tim Singer, Keith Huckins, Thom Rusnak and Andrew Gormley reunite in Brooklyn for a benefit for the family of Rich Hall, the 1000 Knives and CBGB promoter who died in January 2025.
years.xp: The Warsaw bill also had [[From Autumn to Ashes|a6bfadac-d028-4bda-a5b2-e1468f556569]], [[Orange 9mm|66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51]], Harvest and [[Skycamefalling|a8aa0797-dab7-4bcd-a2ef-e5e0fff5f309]]. The next night at Brooklyn Monarch, [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], [[Cave In|f3c95ad4-215b-4519-8660-84c9f467da05]] and [[Deadguy|311e7afe-e0e3-476a-a703-fcd61dc049ac]] played the second Rich Hall show.
